item.title: Cache Proxies for Ephemeral CI Runners
item.description:
ephemerd gives every CI job a brand new runner. A new container on Linux, a new VM on macOS and Windows. The job runs, the runner is thrown away, and the next job starts from a clean image. That is the whole point. Nothing a job does can leak into the next one.

Clean has a cost. A fresh runner has an empty cache. So every job downloads the world again. Go modules, crates, the Rust toolchain, Composer packages, release tarballs. On a busy repo that is gigabytes a day, pulled over and over, most of it byte-for-byte identical to what the last job pulled.

item.title: Rolling Your Own KV Store Instead of Embedding Redis
item.description: Every PHP deployment I’ve run eventually grew a Redis. Sessions, the WordPress object cache, Laravel’s cache and locks, rate limiting. ePHPm is supposed to be one binary that replaces nginx + php-fpm + Redis, so it needed a cache in the box. I didn’t want to write one. This post covers why I did anyway and how it’s built. It also covers the bug that sat in its eviction code from March until last month. Then I compare it against a stock Redis on the same machine with redis-benchmark doing the talking.
